target_customer: Adults with environmental allergies who want to stop daily pills and sprays, paying 99 dollars a month or insurance
problem: Allergy sufferers rely on pills and sprays or inconvenient in-clinic shots. Wyndly delivered sublingual immunotherapy by telehealth with an at-home test and mailed drops.
business_model: Direct to consumer telehealth subscription, plus insurance billing

founders.name: Aakash Shah
founders.background_notes: Led growth engineering at SparkGift (acquired by Stockpile 2016) and Parse.ly (acquired by Automattic 2021) per the YC description.

founders.name: Manan Shah
founders.background_notes: ENT surgeon and telehealth practitioner, cousin of Aakash Shah.

technical_complexity.rationale: Software was a standard telehealth stack. The hard parts were clinical, pharmacy and multi-state licensing operations, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Physician licensing and compounding pharmacy partnerships add friction, but rivals such as Curex offered near identical at-home drops.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found. The company still operates independently with its own site, and partnerships with Amazon One Medical and others are listed.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in February 2021 cited allergy drops as an alternative to shots and daily antihistamines, with the pandemic pushing allergy visits to telemedicine. The YC page cites 60 million Americans with allergies.

branding.name_origin: The company site ties the name to breath and living fully, and a design agency case study says the breeze icon references the name. No founder source on the exact origin.

identity.logo: Breeze icon beside the wordmark suggesting movement and scientific authority, per an agency case study
identity.visual_style: Natural, human photography, deliberately avoiding white background stock images
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, reassuring and clinical, built around the doctor patient relationship

branding.community_and_virality: Press features in TechCrunch, Inc. and The New York Times listed on its site. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive, soft name with a coherent identity and national press, but no evidence of a brand driven growth engine.

outcome_analysis: Wyndly paired a practicing ENT surgeon with a growth engineer and launched allergy drops by telehealth in 38 states at 99 dollars a month during the pandemic telehealth boom. It raised a small seed of about 2 million dollars in February 2023 and still operates under its own brand. YC lists the company as acquired, but no acquisition was found, so the directory status conflicts with the sources read and may reflect an unreported or recent deal.
notes: Directory status is Acquired but the company site shows no acquisition and an outcome search found none, so exit type is recorded as unknown. The 2 million dollar February 2023 round is called a seed by the company blog and Series A by some aggregators, and lead is disputed. A 12 million dollar 2022 Series A on one geo page is rejected as inconsistent. Competitor search returned only 2025 to 2026 pages (Curex, Quello, Nectar), mostly vendor authored, with nothing dated near early 2021, so the list is empty. TechCrunch 2021 does not name competitors.
